cities.name: Leh
cities.overview: Ladakh's main town at about 3,500 m, overlooked by Leh Palace. Spend at least two days here acclimatising before going higher.
cities.history: The capital of the Himalayan kingdom of Ladakh from the 17th century and a major stop on the caravan routes between Tibet, Kashgar and Kashmir. The Namgyal kings built its nine-storey palace.

cities.name: Spangmik
cities.overview: A small village on the shore of Pangong Tso, about 150 km from Leh, with camps and homestays for overnight stays.

cities.name: Diskit
cities.overview: The main village of the Nubra Valley, reached from Leh over the Khardung La pass.

cities.name: Kargil
cities.overview: Ladakh's second town, on the road between Srinagar and Leh, and the gateway to Zanskar.

cities.name: Dras
cities.overview: A cold high town on the Srinagar road, close to the Kargil war memorial.

cities.name: Padum
cities.overview: The small capital of Zanskar, a remote valley reached by a long road.

cities.name: Korzok
cities.overview: A high Changpa village on the shore of Tso Moriri.

places.name: Pangong Tso
places.shortDescription: A long high-altitude lake at about 4,225 m whose water shifts from turquoise to deep blue through the day.
places.description: Pangong Tso stretches for about 134 km across the border between Ladakh and Tibet, with roughly a third of it in India. The road from Leh crosses the Chang La pass at about 5,300 m before the lake appears, its colours changing with the light against bare brown mountains. Camps and homestays at Spangmik and Lukung allow an overnight stay to see the sunrise; nights are cold even in summer. Check the current permit rules with the Ladakh administration before you go.
places.history: The lake is endorheic, with no outflow, and its water is brackish. It freezes completely in winter, when it is sometimes used for ice hockey and a frozen-lake marathon.
places.bestTimeNote: May to September. The lake freezes from about December to March and roads can close after snow.

entryFee.note: Check current permit and environment fee rules with the Ladakh administration.

location.address: Spangmik, Pangong Tso, Leh district, Ladakh

places.name: Thiksey Monastery
places.shortDescription: A hilltop Gelug monastery near Leh, often compared to Lhasa's Potala Palace, with a 15 m Maitreya Buddha.
places.description: Thiksey's whitewashed buildings climb a hill above the Indus valley about 19 km from Leh. The highlight is the temple of Maitreya, the future Buddha, whose seated statue rises about 15 m through two storeys. Arrive early to watch the morning prayers, when monks chant and blow long horns from the roof. The rooftop gives sweeping views of the valley and the Stok range.
places.history: Thiksey was founded in the 15th century and belongs to the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism. The Maitreya statue was installed to mark the Dalai Lama's visit in 1970.
places.bestTimeNote: May to October. The Gustor festival with masked dances is held in autumn.

timings.hours: About 7:00 AM – 6:00 PM; morning prayers around 6:00 AM

highlights: Rooftop views of the Indus valley

places.name: Nubra Valley
places.shortDescription: A high desert valley beyond Khardung La, with sand dunes, double-humped camels and the hilltop Diskit Monastery.
places.description: Nubra lies where the Shyok and Nubra rivers meet, reached from Leh over the Khardung La pass. At Hunder, sand dunes sit beneath snowy peaks and visitors can ride Bactrian (double-humped) camels, descendants of animals from the old Silk Route caravans. Diskit Monastery, the oldest in Nubra, is crowned by a 32 m statue of the Maitreya Buddha facing down the valley. Turtuk, a Balti village near the Line of Control, makes a fascinating extension.
places.history: Nubra was on the trade route between Ladakh, Central Asia and Tibet. Diskit Monastery was founded in the 14th century.
places.bestTimeNote: May to September; Khardung La can close after snowfall.

entryFee.note: Check current permit rules with the Ladakh administration.

places.name: Leh Palace
places.shortDescription: A nine-storey 17th-century royal palace over Leh, modelled on the Potala in Lhasa.
places.description: An empty mud-brick palace on the ridge above the old town, with wooden balconies, small rooms and a wide view from the roof.
places.history: Built around 1600 by King Sengge Namgyal.

places.name: Shanti Stupa
places.shortDescription: A white peace pagoda on a hill above Leh, built with Japanese help, with a sunset view.
places.description: A steep stair or a road leads to the white dome above Changspa. It's the classic place to catch sunset over the valley.

places.name: Hemis Monastery
places.shortDescription: The richest monastery in Ladakh, on the Indus 40 km from Leh, known for its summer masked dance.
places.description: An old Drukpa monastery in a side valley. The two-day Hemis festival brings out masked dances and a giant thangka every summer.

images.credit: Bernard Gagnon Canon EOS REBEL T4i

places.name: Alchi Monastery
places.shortDescription: An 11th-century monastery complex in a riverside village, with rare early Buddhist paintings.
places.description: Small mud temples hold some of the oldest and finest wall paintings in the Himalaya. It's unusually on flat land, not perched on a hill.

places.name: Lamayuru Monastery
places.shortDescription: One of Ladakh's oldest monasteries, perched above a strange moon-like landscape on the Kargil road.
places.description: A dramatic hillside monastery, overlooking eroded rock formations known as Moonland. The Yuru Kabgyat festival fills it with masked dancers.

places.name: Shey Monastery
places.shortDescription: The old summer palace of the Ladakhi kings, 15 km from Leh, with a giant gold-plated Buddha.
places.description: A ruined hilltop palace with a two-storey copper and gilt Buddha statue, close to the Indus.

places.name: Spituk Monastery
places.shortDescription: A monastery above the Indus just 8 km from Leh, right next to the airport.
places.description: A cluster of whitewashed buildings on a rock, one of the first sights you see when flying into Leh.

places.name: Likir Monastery
places.shortDescription: A monastery on a hill in a quiet valley 52 km from Leh, with a large gold Maitreya Buddha.
places.description: A tall golden Maitreya Buddha looks out over a small valley. The monastery was founded in the 11th century.

places.name: Magnetic Hill
places.shortDescription: A stretch of road near Leh where cars seem to roll uphill, thanks to an optical illusion.
places.description: A stop on the Srinagar highway, where drivers put cars in neutral to feel the effect. It's really an optical illusion caused by the landscape.

places.name: Hemis National Park
places.shortDescription: A high-altitude national park near Leh, famous for snow leopards.
places.description: Winter expeditions head into the Rumbak valley to find snow leopards. In summer, its Markha Valley trek is among the best in India.

places.name: Khardung La
places.shortDescription: A famous high road pass 40 km north of Leh, the gateway to the Nubra Valley.
places.description: Snow-covered even in summer, with a small military post and a tea stall at the top. Altitude is a real concern, so don't linger until you've acclimatised.
places.bestTimeNote: Foreign nationals and Indian visitors need permits for this area, usually arranged in Leh.

places.name: Chang La
places.shortDescription: A high pass at 5,360 m on the road to Pangong Tso.
places.description: A bleak saddle with a small temple and army tea stall, crossed on the way to Pangong.
places.bestTimeNote: Foreign nationals and Indian visitors need permits for this area, usually arranged in Leh.

places.name: Diskit Monastery
places.shortDescription: The oldest and largest monastery in Nubra, with a giant Maitreya statue looking down the valley.
places.description: A big hillside monastery with a 32 m statue of the Maitreya Buddha that can be seen from far across the valley.
places.bestTimeNote: Foreign nationals and Indian visitors need permits for this area, usually arranged in Leh.

places.name: Turtuk
places.shortDescription: A Balti village in Nubra close to the Pakistan border, open to visitors only since 2010.
places.description: A green, apricot-growing village with a different language and culture from the rest of Ladakh. It was part of Baltistan until 1971.
places.bestTimeNote: Foreign nationals and Indian visitors need permits for this area, usually arranged in Leh.

places.name: Tso Moriri
places.shortDescription: A high Ramsar-listed lake at 4,522 m in the Changthang, with black-necked cranes and Changpa nomads.
places.description: Deep blue water in a broad, bare valley. It's quieter than Pangong, and Korzok village is the only settlement on its shore.
places.bestTimeNote: Foreign nationals and Indian visitors need permits for this area, usually arranged in Leh.

places.name: Tso Kar
places.shortDescription: A salt lake in the Rupshu Plateau, known for birds and for salt once traded by nomads.
places.description: A shimmering white-edged lake on the way to Tso Moriri. The Thukje village nearby is a stopover.
places.bestTimeNote: Foreign nationals and Indian visitors need permits for this area, usually arranged in Leh.

places.name: Hanle
places.shortDescription: A remote village in the Changthang, with an old monastery, one of the world's highest observatories and dark skies.
places.description: A dark-sky reserve near the Chinese border, centred on the Indian Astronomical Observatory. It's a dream for stargazers.
places.bestTimeNote: Foreign nationals and Indian visitors need permits for this area, usually arranged in Leh.

places.name: Kargil War Memorial
places.shortDescription: The memorial at Dras to the Indian soldiers who died in the 1999 Kargil War.
places.description: A pink sandstone wall lists the names of the dead, with Tololing and Tiger Hill visible behind it. It's a powerful stop on the Srinagar road.
places.history: Built by the Indian Army after the 1999 war with Pakistan.

places.name: Zanskar Valley
places.shortDescription: A remote high valley of Ladakh, known for its frozen-river trek and its old monasteries.
places.description: Reached by a long road past Kargil, with the Chadar trek on the frozen river in winter. Padum is the main town.

places.name: Phugtal Monastery
places.shortDescription: A monastery built like a honeycomb into a cliff cave, in south-east Zanskar, reached only on foot.
places.description: One of the most remote and spectacular monasteries in the Himalaya. It's a long day's walk from the road's end, in the Lungnak Valley.
